author: R. C. Washington
title: Fullerton Medicaid payments for Temporary Codes reach $197,428 in 2024, surging 495%
text:
Fullerton Medicaid payments for Temporary Codes reach $197,428 in 2024, surging 495%
Fullerton Medicaid providers billed $197,428 for services under the Temporary Codes category in 2024, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Medicaid Provider Spending data show. The total rose 495% from 2023, when providers submitted $33,182 in claims for these services.
Medicaid, a state-operated and federally and state-funded public health insurance program, covers low-income people, seniors, children and individuals with disabilities, making it among the largest components of the U.S. health system. More information on funding is available from the Commonwealth Fund.
Because Medicaid is taxpayer funded, shifts in local billing amounts reflect how health care resources are distributed within each community.
The Temporary Codes grouping consists of certain Medicaid-billed services identified according to HCPCS and CPT coding rules. This analysis assigned each billing code to one service category using specific code prefixes and numeric groupings, letting related services be reviewed together without double counting and supporting more accurate rankings over time.
While Medicaid spending increased for several categories of care, Temporary Codes was ranked 14th by payment amount in Fullerton for 2024.
Statewide, Temporary Codes ranked 17th by total Medicaid payments in California during 2024.
During the five years preceding 2024, Fullerton Medicaid payments for Temporary Codes grew by $181,536, or 1,142.3%. Several notable year-over-year jumps, especially in 2021 and 2022, contributed to the category’s growth.
Payments for Temporary Codes services, although distributed across Fullerton, were concentrated in relatively few ZIP codes. In 2024, the largest Medicaid payments tied to Temporary Codes came from ZIP codes 92832—$188,533—and 92835—$8,894. Combined, these top 2 ZIP codes made up 100% of Fullerton’s Temporary Codes Medicaid payments that year.
Within the category, Medicaid payments were localized to a small group of individual billing codes.
In a local context, Fullerton's Medicaid payments for Temporary Codes rose 495% between 2024 and 2023, much higher than the broader 19.8% increase seen across all Medicaid claim categories in the city during that period.
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reported combined federal and state Medicaid spending totaled about $871.7 billion for fiscal year 2023, about 18% of national health expenditures, a significant increase from $613.5 billion in 2019, ahead of the COVID-19 pandemic.
The jump represents an increase of roughly 40% in only a few years, mainly attributed to expanded enrollment and greater utilization during and following the pandemic.
Recent federal budget measures under the Trump administration introduced major proposals to cut federal Medicaid funding and restructure the program. The “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” enacted in 2025, is expected to reduce federal Medicaid spending by more than $1 trillion over the next decade and bring new requirements such as work mandates and increased cost-sharing. These changes could reduce coverage and funding for some enrollees, shift costs to states, and slow federal Medicaid growth, though the program still serves tens of millions across the U.S.
